questions.question:
**A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate word. Choose the correct alternative.**

His heart pounded as he checked his rearview mirror and saw only the dark ________ of highway.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'stretch'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word for the given blank is** 'stretch'.**
 
• The given sentence describes a situation where the protagonist is driving on a highway and feeling anxious about something. The phrase*** "rearview mirror"*** suggests that the protagonist is looking behind him, and the fact that he sees only darkness suggests that he is alone and possibly afraid. In this context, the word "**stretch**" makes the most sense.
 
• The word **"stretch" **means an uninterrupted area or expanse of land, water, or something else.(खींचाव) In this case, it is referring to the uninterrupted length of the highway behind the protagonist. The use of** "dark" **in the sentence suggests that it is night time, and therefore the** "stretch" **of the highway would be difficult to see.
 
• Let's see why other can't be the answers:
 
 
• **Option 1**, "**vitality**," means the state of being strong and active, which does not fit the context of the sentence.(जीवंतता)
 
• **Option 3**, "**trench**," means a long, narrow excavation in the ground, which does not fit the context of the sentence.(खाई)
 
• **Option 4**, "**emancipation**," means the act of being set free from something, which does not fit the context of the sentence.(मुक्ति)
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

**Correct Sentence:__** *His heart pounded as he checked his rearview mirror and saw only the dark **stretch** of highway.*

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P. Within an hour, he was in jail.

Q. He made no attempts to hide his identity and even looked directly into the security camera and smiled.

R. On Jan 6, 1995, McArthur Wheeler boldly robbed two banks in broad daylight with no disguise.

S. By 11:00 at night, his picture was all over the news, leading an informant to identify Wheeler to the police.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'RQSP'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
• **Sentence R** sets the context and describes the event of **McArthur Wheeler** robbing two banks without a disguise.
 
• **Sentence Q** follows and provides an additional detail that he even looked into the security camera and smiled, which shows that he was overconfident and underestimated the consequences of his actions.
 
• Then, **sentence S **provides the consequence of his action that by 11:00 at night, his picture was all over the news, which ultimately led to his identification by an informant to the police.
 
• Finally, **sentence P** concludes the paragraph by stating that he was arrested and put in jail within an hour. 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sequence:__*** On Jan 6, 1995, McArthur Wheeler boldly robbed two banks in broad daylight with no disguise. He made no attempts to hide his identity and even looked directly into the security camera and smiled. By 11:00 at night, his picture was all over the news, leading an informant to identify Wheeler to the police. Within an hour, he was in jail.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

__The man which was present__ at the meeting spoke against the chairperson.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'The man who was present'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'The man who was present' **should be used instead of** 'The man which was present'.**
 
• In the given sentence, **"which"** is incorrect because **"which"** is used **to refer to things or animals, not people.**
 
• Also,** "men" **is incorrect because the sentence refers to one man, not multiple **men**. The correct relative pronoun for a singular subject is** "who," not "whom."**
 
• Thus, as per the above explanation, we can conclude that the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***The man who was present** at the meeting spoke against the chairperson.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__***

 
• **"Who" **and **"whom" **are relative pronouns that are often confused, but they have distinct uses based on the grammatical context.
 
• **"Who" **is used in the **subjective case. **This means it's used when the pronoun acts as the **subject **of a particular clause. In other words, **"who" **is used when the pronoun is doing the action.
 
 
• **Example: **"Jane is the woman **who **baked the cookies." In this sentence, "who" is linked to the action of baking the cookies.
 
 
 
• **"Whom" **is used in the **objective case. **This means it's used when the pronoun acts as the object of a particular clause. **"Whom" **is used when some action is being done to the pronoun.
 
 
• **Example:** "Tom is the man **whom **Jane visited." In this sentence, "whom" is the object of the action "Jane visited."

questions.question:

__
 
• The most appropriate option for the given blank is** 'out of stock'.**
 
• The correct answer is **"out of stock"**.** "Out of stock"** means that the store has run out of the item and does not have it available for sale at the moment.
 
• Let's see why other options can't be the answer:
 
 
• Option 1 **"in fashion" **means that the item is currently trendy or popular.
 
• Option 2 **"in vain"** means that their attempt to get the item was unsuccessful.
 
• Option 4 **"on leave"** means that the store is closed temporarily, usually because the staff is taking time off.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate option to complete the sentence is **"out of stock".**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *They were not able to get the item from the store because it was **out of stock.***** **

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.**

I must tell you that it all __went pear-shaped__ after you left the meeting in the middle.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Went terribly wrong'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom **'went pear-shaped' **is** 'went terribly wrong'.**
 
• The idiom **"went pear-shaped" **means that a situation or event has gone wrong, or has become a failure, unexpected or problematic. It is commonly used in British English.
 
 
• *Example: Our plan to surprise her with a party **went pear-shaped** when she found out beforehand.*

 
 
 

**Correct Answer:__** *Went terribly wrong.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's see the origin of this idiom:
 
 
• The **origin** of this idiom is not certain, but it is believed to have originated in the** British Air Force during the 1940s.**
 
• It was used to describe a plane crash or a mission that had gone awry, and the shape of a plane falling from the sky was similar to the shape of a pear.
 
• Over time, the idiom started to be used in a broader sense to describe any situation that had gone wrong or had not gone according to plan.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

The bus is now full of passengers, it __will leave__ soon.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'is going to leave'.**

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here,** 'is going to leave'** should be used instead of** 'will leave'.**
 
• The sentence talks about the future action of the bus leaving soon.** "Is going to leave" **is **a future continuous tense** that indicates an action that will happen in the near future. Hence, it is the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment.
 
• Let's see why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1**: "**leaves**" is in **'simple present tense'**, which does not fit in the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "is leaving" **is **'present continuous tense'**, which can be used to indicate an action that is happening currently. However, in the given sentence, the bus is not leaving currently, but it will leave soon in the future.
 
• **Option 4: "has to leave"** is in **'present perfect tense'**, which indicates a completed action in the past that has a connection to the present. It does not fit in the context of the sentence, as the sentence talks about the future action of the bus leaving soon.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** The bus is now full of passengers, it **is going to leave soon.***** **

questions.question:

options.text: Where do he find this pen?
Where does he find this pen?

questions.solution:

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of Passive Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it to Active Voice. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• In the 'active-passive' transformation except for (who and whom) rest of the Wh-family Pronouns will remain unchanged. 
 
• Here, the given question 'Where' will remain unchanged.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• 'was found' will be changed into 'did find'. 

 
 
 

Correct Sentence:__ *Where did he find this pen?*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.**

Kranthi loves to swim at the local swimming pool __in order that relieve__ his work stress.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'in order to relieve'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'in order to relieve' **should be used instead of** 'in order that relieve'.**
 
• The phrase** 'in order that' **is used to introduce the purpose or the reason for something. It is followed by a clause that explains the **purpose**.
 
• In the given sentence, the purpose of Kranthi swimming at the local swimming pool is to relieve his work stress. So, we need a phrase that can convey the purpose. **Option 4)** **'in order to relieve' **correctly conveys the purpose of Kranthi swimming at the local swimming pool.
 
• Let's see why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1) 'in order which'** is incorrect as '**which**' cannot be used to introduce the purpose of something.
 
• **Option 3) 'in order as to relieve' **is grammatically incorrect as the phrase **'in order as to'** is not used in **English**.
 
 
 
• Therefore, **option 4)** is the correct answer.

**Correct Sentence:__** *Krathi loves to swing at the local swimming pool **in order to relieve** his work stress.*

questions.question:
